group_assessment.weighting: A multi-centre clinical-genetics consortium reporting a retrospective diagnostic-laboratory series, and the senior author's single WWOX publication. There is no experimental arm of any kind: every statement in the paper is a clinical observation or a variant call. That is the right provenance for a phenotype and endpoint question and the wrong provenance for a mechanism, which is how the reading uses it - no mechanistic proposition is taken from it.

queue.target: Piard et al. 2019 - the comparator cohort this paper measures itself against on four endpoints (age at seizure onset, respiratory involvement, growth retardation and microcephaly rates, eye contact)
queue.question: Does the comparator cohort quantify any of these endpoints with an instrument, or are its rates counts of qualitative descriptors too? The disagreements this paper reports - 80 percent against 40 percent respiratory, its own near-universal failure to thrive against 6 percent growth retardation - are interpretable only if both cohorts ascertained the endpoint the same way.
queue.status: open - that cohort is held and read in this repository, so the question is asked of the existing reading, not of a new acquisition

queue.target: Havali et al. 2021 - head circumference below -3 SD in all six patients of another cohort
queue.question: Is that a measured series of occipitofrontal circumferences with ages, i.e. a usable growth-endpoint denominator for WOREE, or a count of a clinical label? Cited here and read nowhere in this repository.

queue.target: Johannsen 2018, Ko 2018, Riva 2022 - the three prior ketogenic-diet reports this paper cites as 'varying degrees of success'
queue.question: What endpoint did each use, over what window, with what exposure denominator? Three citations carrying the word success are the whole published base of the only dietary early-benefit observation in WOREE, and none of the three is read for its diet arm here.
queue.status: open - the highest-value queue item this reading produces

queue.target: Repudi et al. 2021 - cited by this paper as the proof of concept for WWOX gene therapy
queue.question: None new. Noted only because a clinical series imports a preclinical rescue as a proof of concept; that rescue's comparator limits are held in this repository and are neither strengthened nor weakened by being cited here.

acquisition_recipe.no_recipe: No route can be shown for these bytes and none is invented. The payload was fetched by an earlier session (2026-09-29) through a publisher gateway whose endpoint, HTTP method and User-Agent policy that session did not record, and this reading made no gateway call: paper_packet.py reported the file as 'on disk and undeclared' and it is declared here for the first time. What the payload itself records is kept instead of a reconstructed URL - its provenance block names source 'scholar_gateway', retrieved_at 2026-09-29T21:18:33.650Z, the query as executed, and two disclosures that travel with every quotation taken from it: 'Results retrieved by Wiley Scholar Gateway' and 'Summary generated by AI - verify claims against source documents'. It delivers 8 of the article's chunks (indices 0, 1, 2, 18, 22, 23, 24, 25). Every quotation in this manifest is article text from a chunk body, never the gateway's summary field, and every locator names its chunk. A replay is therefore not reproducible from this manifest, which is a declared gap and the reason the derived text artefact below carries the full extractor call.

acquisition_recipe.note: Concatenates the delivered chunk bodies in ascending chunk_index under '===== CHUNK n =====' headers, with no normalisation of the chunk text itself. It exists so the locators below verify against bytes rather than against a JSON escape form; the propositions were read on the chunk bodies, which are the same characters.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: The source is not a full text and is not indexed as one: 8 chunks of the article are present and chunk indices 3-17 and 19-21 are absent, so no section can be asserted complete. Each entry names the chunk it came from. Table 1 is delivered twice, in chunks 2 and 18, which is why several snippets occur twice in the derived text.
verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: The abstract of this paper is three sentences of phenotype summary and carries none of the propositions below. It names the ketogenic diet once, as 'epilepsy that responded to a ketogenic diet in three patients', and that sentence is the overstatement this reading exists to bound: it carries no endpoint, no exposure denominator, no window, no comparator and no developmental outcome, and the abstract contains no EEG, growth, visual, sleep or mortality value at all. Anchoring these entries to it would attach each measured bound to the sentence it narrows.

entries.proposition: The ketogenic-diet benefit in this cohort is a clinician-reported improvement in seizure control in three named patients, with no counted, scored or instrumented endpoint behind the word 'improved'.
entries.snippet: However, the institution of a ketogenic diet in patients 1, 2, and 4 notably improved seizure control.

entries.proposition: The authors themselves decline to assert a beneficial effect of the diet, and name cohort size as the reason.
entries.snippet: It may be premature to assert the potential beneficial effects of a ketogenic diet as they need to be evaluated carefully in a larger cohort.

entries.proposition: Developmental status is identical across all five columns, the three diet responders included: in this series the symptomatic observation and the developmental outcome do not move together.
entries.snippet: |Developmental delay |Profound developmental delay |Profound developmental delay |Profound developmental delay |Profound developmental delay |Profound developmental delay |

entries.proposition: Growth in this cohort is reported as SD scores and percentiles for occipitofrontal circumference, height and weight at a stated age - a quantitative, repeatable, clinically obtainable measurement, and the only human WOREE endpoint of that kind in the records this repository holds.

Weight: 1.5 SD

entries.declared_surface_defect: The minus signs are absent from this extracted surface. The three values are read here as the MAGNITUDES of SD scores and not as signed numbers: the direction comes from the row's own context, the same table calling this patient microcephalic from two months, and not from the characters quoted. Same class of defect as an exponent flattened by an extraction route. No proposition in this reading uses the sign, and a reading that needs it must open the typeset table.

entries.proposition: A visual evoked potential was performed in one WOREE patient of this series and was undetectable bilaterally - so a VEP does exist as a performed measurement in WOREE, qualitatively and at n = 1.
entries.snippet: Patient 4 demonstrated undetected visual evoked potentials suggesting central involvement.

entries.proposition: A sleep study was performed in one patient of this series and detected sleep apnoea with hypopnoea - so polysomnography also exists as a performed measurement in WOREE, at n = 1, with no parameter reported.
entries.snippet: |Sleep apnea with hypopnea detected by sleep study |
entries.anchor: Table 1, row 'Respiratory features', second column; delivered in chunks 2 and 18

entries.proposition: EEG in this cohort is a qualitative pattern description in every column - hypsarrhythmia, background slowing, multifocal discharges - with no quantitative parameter, no discharge density, no background score and no repeat interval.
